result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both screenshots show only the top of each page, so the type and spacing scales and the sample form, card and status message could not be checked; scores for items 1, 3 and 4 are estimates from what is visible. B gets the edge because it sets up color explicitly by role ('Components use roles, never raw ramp values'), maps light and dark themes onto the same role names, checks contrast in both themes and links to a section on how to change the system. A has clear, short rules ('Tokens only… Add a token first') and a warm light palette that suits a clinic slightly better, but in the visible part its color section starts as 'Brand and neutrals', which reads more like a list of hues than a set of jobs. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both screenshots show only the top of the page, so neither the sample pieces nor the token scales can be checked, and those scores are moderate guesses. B's warm light neutrals, deep teal and evenly aligned layout feel more like a calm, trustworthy clinic, and its numbered build rules (tokens only, never color alone, one primary action) are short and easy to act on. A has good principles and organizes color by role with light and dark themes, but it opens in a heavy dark theme and its hero text sits out of line with the sections below.
